newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt agrees spending cuts of 50 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt agrees spending cuts of 50 mln punts.

text.p: The Irish government on Thursday agreed on spending cuts of 50 million Irish pounds to pay for the settlement of a nurses' dispute.

Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn told Irish state radio that a cabinet budget sub-committee met this morning and identified the reductions in spending. Its decisions should be signed off as a formality at a cabinet meeting next week.

Quinn said every government department was making a contribution on a pro rata basis toward meeting the 49 million Irish pounds needed to settle the nurses' pay claim and prevent strike action which would have seriously disrupted Ireland's healthcare services.

Some 20-25 million would be saved on social welfare spending, he said, noting that the government has provided for a sum of money to deal with unemployment but the good performance of the economy meant it wouldn't all be needed.
But Quinn also warned that other groups of workers should not think they could start to make additional or new pay claims on foot of the nurses's dispute.
"There is no magic pot of money under the table and it will come off existing expenditure provision," he said.

Quinn also said such leap-frogging claims could damage the strong performance of the Irish economy and threaten his ability to deliver tax cuts of 900 million Irish pounds over a three-year period as agreed in the recent national wage accord, Partnership 2000.

"The economy is doing well because everybody is playing as a team. If anybody, as in any team, starts to get selfish and wants to hold onto the ball for themselves, not only will be not score goals but we will be relegated out of the successful top of the league where we are at the present time," he said.
